title: Pulse backpressure resolver and quiet-window stabilizer for regional failovers
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces a pulse-based backpressure resolver and a quiet-window stabilizer to reduce oscillation during regional failovers; safe rollouts with feature flag and gradual traffic ramp; instrumentation for incident analysis.
description:
Motivation: During a recent partial-region outage we observed rapid oscillation where nodes would flip between evicted and healthy states and cause cascading rejoin storms (INC-2026-02-12). Root cause tracing showed noise in short-term health signals plus immediate reopen attempts triggered by transient probe successes. This PR implements a different approach: rather than a single-point health threshold, we aggregate a short-duration pulse of health/latency signals and apply a hysteresis+quiet-window so reopen candidate nodes/tenants observe a short stabilization window before acceptance.

What this PR does: single continuous change set with feature-flagged rollout. Key changes: 1) pulse_resolver: new component that collects a 5-30s sliding pulse of probe/latency/burst metrics and computes a damped health score (per-tenant weighting supported). 2) quiet_window: a configurable holdoff applied after any circuit transition; windows support exponential backoff and a max cap to avoid permanent quarantine. 3) tenant_damping: per-tenant damping factors to avoid noisy micro-tenants triggering global oscillation; defaults tuned conservatively. 4) kv_preserve_hotfix: small hotfix to prevent premature KV cache eviction during soft rejoin paths (incident regression). 5) telemetry: new metrics and trace spans (pulse_score, quiet_window_start, quiet_window_expire, tenant_damp) and dashboards preconfigured for the console. 6) tests: unit tests for pulse scoring math, e2e integration in the failover simulator, and chaos scenario reproducer.

Files touched (high level): list below shows representative files modified/added. Small illustrative snippets are in the code body but diffs kept compact. The design follows the existing circuit state machine and reuses the region coordinator API.

Design notes and rationale: The pulse approach trades sub-second sensitivity for stability across regional handoffs. We found in the incident trace that immediate reopen attempts within 10s were responsible for >60% of oscillation events. By aggregating a short pulse (configurable per deployment) and applying a quiet window before accepting a state change we get much lower flip rates while still enabling recovery. The per-tenant damping lets high-frequency noisy tenants be typed differently from low-volume customers.

Testing and canary plan: - Feature flag: rollout behind `enable_pulse_resolver` and `enable_quiet_window`. - Canary region: deploy to staging then eu-west-1 (10% traffic) then us-west-2 (25% traffic) over 48 hours. - Metrics to watch: circuit_flip_rate, pulse_score_hist, regional_rejoin_rate, kv_eviction_rate. - Automated rollback: if circuit_flip_rate goes above historical baseline + 30% for 15m, flag rolls back automatically.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for pulse scoring and quiet window timers - [x] Integration test in failover simulator - [x] Added telemetry and dashboard wiring - [x] Hotfix for KV premature clear included - [x] Feature flags and canary plan documented

Commits summary: See commits list for granular history. Each commit focuses on a small area to ease review and bisecting.

Related: ENG-8215 (decrease oscillation), ENG-8229 (post-incident followup), INC-2026-02-12.

Migration/Config: Defaults are conservative; no rollout without explicit enablement. New config options in region coordinator: pulse_window_seconds (default 15), pulse_decay_alpha (default 0.6), quiet_window_base_seconds (default 10), quiet_window_max_seconds (default 600), tenant_damp_map (optional).

Operational notes: Added alerts and dashboard that link directly to the failover simulator trace so on-call can reproduce and verify behavior before changing flags in prod.

Merge decision: merged via squash after two approving reviews and successful CI with canary integration tests.
